items.question: A cart of constant mass moves right. A constant nonzero net force acts right. Which explanation describes what happens next?

options.text: Its speed stays exactly constant because the force maintains its existing motion.
Its speed rises equally each second because the force produces constant acceleration.
Its speed rises more each second because the force produces increasing acceleration.

items.question: A 3 kg cart moves left. Its mass is constant and its net force is 12 N right. Which argument justifies an acceleration of 4 m/s² right?

options.text: F_net = ma gives a = 12/3 = 4 m/s²; acceleration points along the velocity.
F_net = ma gives a = 12/3 = 4 m/s²; acceleration points opposite the net force.
F_net = ma gives a = 12/3 = 4 m/s²; acceleration points along the net force.
